lines.text: My slow self is the bottleneck, but I'm still moving fast and smart overall.
[GPT5.icon]

In a world where AI moves much faster, we need to abandon the assumption that we control the process by ourselves while understanding it all. Humans will become designers of objectives, constraints, and evaluation axes, rather than process supervisors, leaving the AI to explore, implement, and self-document (log, summarize, version control), with another AI in charge of testing and reviewing as well. Humans would periodically check only the output and decide "what to consider a problem" and "what meaning to give to which proposal. Even if you can't fully grasp the process, you only need to have a grip on the entry, exit, and rewind mechanisms. You cannot change the fact that you are slow, but there is no need to slow down the entire process because of your slowness. You are the bottleneck, but if you use your slowness as a filter, you can move faster and smarter as a whole.
[https://gyazo.com/6068456f18d27c4f25e7263deab8e526]
A: Before AI, humans moved slower, so there was more scope for grasping
B: With the advent of AI, the speed at which human-AI pairs moved increased, but the speed was still within the grasp of humans
The extent of the "graspable range" may vary from person to person
May differ from task to task.
C: And then it accelerates even further, beyond what we can grasp, to the point where people say, "What? What do you mean?" and it's like, "Oh, what?
It's a mistake for humans and AI to keep pace in the first place.
D: AI should use its high speed to search outside the range of human observation
We can then suggest to the human, "After studying Proposals 1, 2, and 3, I think that Proposal 3 is promising, so let's take this course of action.
People can say no to that, of course.
I could say explore more ideas like this.
[** latitude]
[nishio.icon]
[https://gyazo.com/82fb8fc67dfd45134df0b0ba495e1edf]
When AI accelerates [ideas] and they go outside [the range of human grasp], we don't know how to bring them back because we haven't [grasped] them.
Isn't it correct to rate something that moves faster than you at your own speed?
How can I make sure that I, as a slow being, don't become a bottleneck?
[GPT5.icon]

It would be easier to sort out the "problem of slow self-discipline of fast things" and the "problem of not being able to return to it once you can no longer grasp it" if they were handled separately.
1. separate roles: don't make it a goal to "understand it all".
❌ A human being keeps track of every single thing that is happening.
✅ Humans hold "objectives and constraints" and "evaluations" and AI moves at high speed toward them.
2. mandate "[compression for humans]" for fast processes
Create a layered structure
L0: Raw trace (read by AI)
L1: Short, step-by-step summary
L2: Human-readable "progress report" in one minute
L3: A human being can read in 10 minutes, "Summary of Background and Implications."
You usually only see L2 or L3.

But if you can "dig to L1/L0 only where you are interested," you can expand only where you need to, assuming you don't follow the whole thing, so it is less likely to break down even if there is a speed difference.
3. "Can't revert" problems can be resolved by version control.
The reason it is difficult to know how to revert is because it is unclear where to start and where to end a "certain single change".
4. let the fast ones audit each other ([let AI audit AI])
5. focus human work on "orienting" and "making sense
AI: Mass generation, search, trial and error
Humans:.
What is considered a problem (problem setting)
Which indicators to focus on (design of evaluation axes)
Making sense of the ideas that emerged, making narratives, and connecting them to society

Only a human being can say not only "Which proposal did you adopt?" but also "Why this proposal?" and "What does it mean to you?" Only a human being can do this, so we intentionally reserve this part as a human task.

6-Pack of Care — Institute for Ethics in AI

The objective is to rethink [AI Alignment] as a "[relational process]" from the perspective of [Ethics of Care] and [Plurality], and to envision a civic AI ([Civic AI]) that promotes [horizontal collaboration].

Six principles (Attentiveness/Responsibility/Competence/Responsiveness/Solidarity/Symbiosis) are presented as "core muscle groups" for multiple entities to cooperate. The six principles are presented as "core muscle groups" for cooperation among multiple entities.
Alignment is positioned as alignment to a credible deliberative and collaborative process (alignment-by-process) rather than optimization to a fixed goal.
The metaphor of "[local god] (kami)" indicates that AI should have sufficiency ([enoughness]) and [exitability] rooted in relationships rather than an expansionist orientation.
Referring to vTaiwan and other experiments and discussions on cooperative AI, [joint creation] ([co-production]) and [citizen participation] will be placed at the center.
6-Pack of Care: A Manifesto — Institute for Ethics in AI
Proposes "[Civic Care]" based on asymmetry because faster AI makes [utilitarianism]/[obligatory ethics] vulnerable.
The digital democracy in Taiwan since 2014 (Polis, etc.) is presented as an example of an implementation that transforms division into "overlap".
[Alignment Assembly] case studies (e.g., against fraudulent advertising) show that deliberation + AI support can lead to a high degree of consensus building and legal institutionalization.
Policy levers proposed include separation of expression and proliferation, social portability, transparency of bridging indicators, and federal-style Trust & Safety.
As a solution to the "is-ought problem," the six principles are reduced to design principles based on an ethic of care rooted in a [thick context].
Prospects for "[horizontal superintelligence] ([We, the People])" with local AI groups rather than a single superintelligence.
Chapter 1: Attentiveness in Recognition — Institute for Ethics in AI
The whole foundation of the project is to fairly determine "what to focus on" first, and visualization of the relationship is the starting point.
Emphasizes the incorporation of accountability, objection, and independent oversight, underlining basic human rights.
Bridging maps and receipt receipts make the voices of minorities and affected populations visible and modifiable.
Emphasis is placed on designing important rules to be reversible and on mechanisms that allow rollback if errors are made.
As an example, a disaster relief bot is used to illustrate the cycle of hearing, mapping, equitable allocation of attention, objection, and restoration.
Chapter 2: Responsibility in Engagement — Institute for Ethics in AI
The core is the Engagement Contract, a promise that clearly states "who will be compensated, by when, to what extent, and how."
Deviations should be disclosed on an "adopt-or-explain" basis, with the supervisory authority having the right to suspend and compensate.
Turn "paper promises" into effective promises with escrows, penalties, audit logs, etc.
Fractalization of responsibilities by Participation Officer (PO) to ensure institutional continuity.
Example of a disaster assistance bot, embodying SLAs, rollback conditions, compensation, and handover.
Chapter 3: Competence in Action — Institute for Ethics in AI
Since competence is proven by operation, not design, we propose a phased introduction of shadow operations, canaries, and public access.
Bridging scores and RLCF (Community Feedback-derived reinforcement learning) reward cooperation over anger.
Emphasis on transparent tracing, repeatable evaluations, and coding of rights guardrails.
Observability and drift monitoring to localize failures and turn them into learning.
Chapter 4: Responsiveness in Adaptation — Institute for Ethics in AI
The core is to keep the restoration loop going by making objections "cheap and fast.
The community itself creates evaluation indicators (Wiki Evals), and the design reflects victims' perspectives in the evaluation.
Publicize incident response logs and translate remediation results into tests to prevent recurrence.
The restoration must always provide either an "explanation or correction" and be completed with a deadline.
Chapter 5: Solidarity in Community — Institute for Ethics in AI
Design the entire ecosystem so that collaboration is the "easiest option.
Agent ID with [melonimity] ([partial anonymity]) to protect privacy while indicating responsibility.
Social portability and interoperability to compete on quality of care, not lock-in.
Avoid single gatekeeper dependence through federal Trust & Safety sharing.
Chapter 6: Symbiosis in Horizon — Institute for Ethics in AI
Instead of a single AI, a federally coordinated ecosystem of local "gods of care (kami)" is proposed.
Limits on objectives, resources, and duration are bound by contract and technology to reduce expansion orientation.
Complementarity is defined in treaties (protocols) and problems are solved locally as much as possible (subsidiarity).
Institutionalize the possibility of exit by incorporating sunset and succession as success requirements.
Chapter 7: Frequently Asked Questions — Institute for Ethics in AI
He presented countermeasures to market militarization, including interoperability, public options, proof of origin for advertising, governance of mission fixes, and alignment assemblies.
He recommends a research ecosystem in which multiple local kami cooperate, rather than one in which results are supreme, as in "curing cancer."
He explained that Civic AI is not a panacea, but a framework to support the formation of common infrastructure and local bridges.
In communities of low trust, poverty, and violence, he emphasized the need to build small, locally driven bridges rather than external "solutions.
Emphasis on transparent processes, bridge indicators, and exit rights to prevent "agenda imposition in the name of good will."

pages.title: Motivation caused by lack of information

lines.text: Motivation caused by lack of information

In a time when people did not share the feeling of those who had what they did not have, they felt that having something that they did not have would make them very happy, and this caused a strong motivation to have it.
With the development of [information sharing], this "[motivation] caused by [lack of information]" will decrease.
[the grass is always greener on the other side]
For example, marriage

In an era when all the older women around them were married, older women would say things like, "Marriage is a woman's happiness," and unmarried women who heard this would have a fear that they would be very unhappy if they didn't get married, and I think this gave them a very strong motivation to get married.

The development of social networking has shared that unmarried arabs are not very unhappy and that married people are not full of happiness, and marriage or not has turned into a choice where you can choose both.
For example, rich people
In the days when things like Hikakin's videos of him buying foreign cars and such were only aired on TV in those areas, there was a strong admiration for rich celebrities and a desire to be one too.

However, if information is also shared about Hikakin's daily work style that would be "extremely black labor if he were a company employee," more people will have the feeling that they don't want to work that hard and want to live a leisurely life.
When you can observe people on social media who have money but seem unhappy, etc., the appeal of having money diminishes.
In the first place, there is a diminishing utility, so getting too much will not make you happy.
I think this change is irreversible.
Like [law of increasing entropy].

lines.text: Easy to follow a little behind.
Can't keep up with the fast changes?
Easy to follow a little behind.
[https://gyazo.com/322f3e55deaf3224f5637a3c094fc90d]
[Is it true that [change is so fast] that you can't keep up, that you get left behind?
Mr. A is trying to keep up with the changes.
I pay a cost of 16 to pick them all up.
Mr. B is paying a cost of 8 because he can't allocate that much cost, and sometimes he's not able to take it down.
1 in 2 times, 1 step behind, average 0.5
Mr. C has a lower cost, paying a cost of 4.
0~3 steps behind, average 1.5
Mr. D pays a cost of 2, 0~7 steps late, average 3.5
Mr. E doesn't pay the cost at all, he pays the cost only once every 16 steps, an average delay of 7.5
How much will Mr. E pay to catch up?
Not 16, looks like not even 1, but maybe not that big, maybe 1.5~3 (appropriate skin feeling).
The question of whether people who catch up every N times pay O(N) costs or O(1) costs.
I have a feeling that it's probably O(log N).

In this way, no matter how fast the state-of-the-art is advancing, those who keep up with it can always catch up faster than the state-of-the-art because they can catch up at a lower cost, and "keeping up" will never happen.
If by "not keeping up" you mean being on the cutting edge, then you're not keeping up.
Easy to follow a little behind the cutting edge
The magnitude of the disadvantages of delay
Determined by the competitive environment
If you're competing with the rest of the world to be the first to achieve results, you have to do A because you can't afford to fall behind your competition.

pages.title: Influences formed outside of our field of vision

lines.text: Influences formed outside of our field of vision

>[weiwei882288 https://x.com/weiwei882288/status/2003474806793240814] Historically in Japanese society, while making a sharp distinction between "inside (seima)" and "outside (world)," in effect "[seima]" was almost all the world needed for survival. The geographical conditions of an island nation, a single language, and a single culture made it difficult to survive. Under the geographical conditions of an island nation, a monolingual society, and a social structure based on village communities, there was little need to constantly negotiate with other civilizations, and [the world's opinion] = [the world] was everything. Thus, "[seima]" functioned well enough as a substitute for the original world, and the Japanese did not need to develop a metacognition to perceive the world in a relative manner.

> Since the Meiji era, Japan joined the international community as a modern nation, introducing diplomacy based on international law and a global capitalist economy. However, although the institutions and formalities were modernized, the assumptions of people's cognition were not updated, and the sense that "the world = the world" remained preserved. As a result, it became easier to apply Japan's internal common sense and logic directly to the outside world, treating foreigners and other cultures not as "subjects of the world" but as "objects that can be evaluated and processed according to internal standards. The very idea of ascertaining what kind of [log], [network], and [influence] an outsider has is weak.

> Furthermore, in Japanese society, influence is easily understood as something visible and within the system, such as titles, organizations, and seniority. On the other hand, influence in the contemporary world is often quietly formed outside of Japanese people's [view], such as in [informal] [diaspora networks] and [professional communities], from online to offline, across borders and languages. Because it is impossible to imagine these "[invisible] influences" only from within the Japanese "[world]," we tend to disregard and exclude foreigners who are not adapted to the context of Japanese society, as well as others who appear to be unknown. As a result, they unknowingly make enemies of those who have influence in another coordinate system, and this structure will later rebound back to their reality in a detrimental way.
I think I understood something close to this through a different route.
Just as there is the world as the inner world and the world as the outer world, there is the internal world and the external world.

At a time when I didn't know how to build my reputation in the internal world, being recognized outside the company made me think, "I don't have to worry too much about my reputation in the internal world.
Originally, the PhD was an evaluation axis that didn't fit within the confines of a particular company.
Experts tend to have professional communities outside the company
Operate in areas outside the company that are not yet very visible from within the company, gain influence, and then come back with something of value to the company.
In 2025, Audrey Tang came to Cybozu's Nihonbashi office and shot a video interview with the president as a clear example.
In 2012 [The birth of the Cybozu Method], we introduced our culture to the outside world, and the outside world recognized our efforts.
This had the effect of strengthening their influence within the company after the fact.

>[weiwei882288 https://x.com/weiwei882288/status/2003474806793240814] While the Western "culture of guilt" presupposes an internalized conscience, the Japanese "culture of shame" -- Ruth Benedict's classic analysis -- takes the public gaze as the absolute arbiter.

> In this structure, morality and justice become synonymous with public approval. The principle of action is not "whether it is right" but "how the world sees it. This leads to strong social integration, but at the same time it makes imagination about the outside of the world unnecessary. Since the world is everything, evaluations outside the world are irrelevant.

> Herein lies the origin of the epistemological fallacy that "the world = the world. Japanese people are extremely sensitive to the evaluation of the "world," but structurally insensitive to the evaluation of the "world" outside the "world" (non-Japanese language speech space, diaspora networks crossing national borders, specialized communities unrelated to ethnic units, etc.). ) is structurally insensitive to the "world" outside of the "between. This is because historically it has not been associated with "worldliness" as it relates to survival and recognition.
[GPT5.icon]
The claim of the presenting post is largely,

Historically in Japan, "inside = the world" was almost all that existed in the world of life, and since worldly affairs/exclusion determined life and death, there was little need to relativize the "outside = the world".

After the Meiji era, only the system was modernized and the assumption of recognition (the world = global sense) remained, so external influences (cross-border networks, etc.) were overlooked and landmines were stepped on.
This can be explained by the "culture of shame/culture of sin" (Benedict).
...I think that is the line of reasoning. If you look at it critically, the weaknesses are rather clear.
The historical narrative is "too strong."

The "island nation, single language, village community → poor constant negotiations with different civilizations" is easy to understand in one aspect, but it is a rough generalization. Even in the Edo period, external trade (Nagasaki) and diplomacy (e.g., Korean envoys) continued, and "the country as a whole was not connected to the outside world" is easily an overstatement. ([Nippon https://www.nippon.com/en/features/c00104/foreign-relations-in-early-modern-japan-exploding-the-myth-of-national-seclusion .html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(Rather, the point of contention would be "who had contact with the outside world = bias in hierarchy/region.")
There is an image of "Japan = the same old Japanese only for everyone," but in reality, it was much messier than that.
Big difference in dialects

In the past, regional differences were stronger than now, and there were situations where mutual understanding was difficult even with the same "Japanese" (i.e., internal "translation" was necessary).
There are minority languages
For example, there are different languages within Japan, such as Ryukyuan and Ainu (i.e., there are "different cultures" within Japan).
Some foreign words.
Certain segments of the population were involved with foreign languages, such as Chinese and Dutch (i.e., not zero negotiations with the outside world).
The assumption that "the world" is monolithic is dangerous.

However, in reality, there can be different "worlds" for different statuses, regions, genders, etc., and the world itself changes with modernization, migration, and industrial structure. In fact, there is a cautious argument that "each world" can exist according to status, region, gender, etc., and that the nature of the world itself changes with modernization, migration, and industrial structure. ([hokuriku-u.ac.jp https://www.hokuriku-u.ac.jp/library/libraryDATA/kiyo55/econ01.pdf])
From this perspective, it is more likely to be a question of which of several worlds is being referred to, rather than the "world = world fallacy.
The "culture of shame/culture of sin" is useful, but academically it's a knife.

The Benedictine framework itself can easily become a "blunt instrument of dichotomy" and is often criticized; Lummis critically discusses the strong influence of "[The Chrysanthemum and the Sword]" as a political document (rather than an accurate statement) and the mass production of dichotomous tools. ([Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus https://apjjf.org/c-douglas-lummis/2474/article])

There are also early criticisms (references to Dore and others) of the "shame-type/guilt-type" division of comparative culture itself. ([J-STAGE https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jsr1950/27/4/27_4_63/_article])
Therefore, it is easy to slip into "Nihonjinron-ish essentialism" when this framework is used as the main engine.
Meaning of "slippery slope to Japenological essentialism."
Essentialism:
To treat the Japanese as if they have a fixed essence (Japanese are this kind of race/ethnicity).
Nihonjinron-like:
A type of argument that broadly states "Japan is special" or "Japanese people are like this."
The biggest one is the "leap of causality.
"Poor negotiation with the outside world" → "Metacognition is not developed."
"shame-centered" → "can't imagine outside influences"

This leap cannot be asserted without psychological and sociological data. As an explanation, it is fascinating, but the weak verifiability (ambiguous disproving conditions) makes it difficult for the argument to be more than a "sticking story".
Some alternative explanations are more straightforward.
"Missing the world's appreciation" is more than the essence of culture, for example.
Language barriers and bias in information distribution
Degree to which careers and resource allocation are closed in the domestic system (academia, government, and business)
Incentives to rationalize optimization for domestic use
Many things can be explained by If you don't hold this point, the story will be moralized like a "flaw of the Japanese people".
Summary: How to rephrase it to make it stronger
This assertion is sharp as a general statement: "If you optimize for a closed evaluation system (the world), you will have accidents in another evaluation system (the world).

However, if we do not focus on ethnic characteristics such as "Japanese people are not able to do this," but rather include (1) the multilayered nature of the world, (2) differences in time, class, and region, and (3) incentives and the information environment, the resistance to criticism will increase dramatically.

The old year passed amidst the sound of firecrackers,
The spring breeze brings warmth and fills the slaughterhouse wine.

Spring breeze sending warmth into the slaughterhouse.

pages.title: Reflection Report on the Deliberation: Considering a Push Social Security System

lines.text: Reflection Report on the Deliberation: Considering a Push Social Security System
Dear Mr. Nishio

Thank you very much for participating in this discussion on "Push Social Security System". From the detailed responses and free descriptions of all 30 items provided by Mr. Nishio, it clearly emerged that he values the two major pillars of **"trust in digital rationality" and "respect for the individual's right to self-determination "**.
I would like to unpack the unique value of NISHIO-sama's perspective in this deliberation by comparing it to the discussions in the various rooms thus far.
1. nishio's point of view: Expectations of digital "fairness

While many participants are prone to concerns about misinformation and cold-bloodedness regarding "digitization and AI use by the government," Nishio's answers show a very positive and consistent rationale.

High trust in "judgment by AI": The respondents strongly agreed that "a uniform judgment by AI is fairer and more reliable than a subjective judgment by an administrative contact. This is a viewpoint that goes one step further than the opinion expressed in past Room 3 and other surveys that "human responses tend to break down due to exception handling," and sharply highlights the core benefit of digitization: "Because it is a machine, fairness is ensured without being influenced by any particular bias.

A pragmatic approach to "mistakes": You clearly disagree with the opinion that "the slightest mistake should not be introduced." I feel that this is a sign of a sense of balance that emphasizes the "pragmatism" of preventing omissions from receiving benefits even if there is some risk, rather than [stagnation due to perfectionism] (continuation of the application-based system).
2. in-depth point: self-determination and system harmonization
The key to "deliberation" in Nishio's response, in particular, is the astute use of **"be bold in your system and cautious in your judgment "**.

Individual Will in "Initial Settings": While agreeing with the collective management and push-type notification using their own number, the respondents are opposed to "making the initial settings shared-on (opt-out method)". From this, we can see a strong commitment to "individuals choosing the system based solely on their own will (placing emphasis on expressing their will at the entrance), rather than the government deciding on its own.

Clear boundary between "notification" and "coercion": While it is "acceptable" to "send" AI distress forecasts, it is emphasized that "the final application should be left to the individual's own will". This seems to be a attempt to reconcile the issue of "stigma (shame and negative labels)" discussed in Room 4 with the "freedom not to be interfered with" ("the right to be left alone"), in which "information is provided, but the individual is free to accept it and act on it".
3. seeds of dialogue with other participants (questions for cessation)
Nishio's flat perspective provides a logical solution to the "emotional concerns" that other participants tend to have. The following points are issues I would like to discuss further next time.
Third-Party Audits: NISHIO questioned the effectiveness of audits, which are subjectively conducted by a third party. On the other hand, "lack of trust in government" was a major barrier in Room 5.
Question: what kind of "auditing mechanism" could be used to prove that the "AI code (algorithm)" is fair, without relying on human subjectivity (emotion and discovery)?

Means that rely on human subjectivity would not be proof in the first place, there needs to be public disclosure of internal algorithms and quantitative experiments to see what output they produce for what kind of data.[nishio.icon]
Priority of "face-to-face contact": While opposing [limiting face-to-face contact to the digitally vulnerable], they agree that the budget should be allocated to companion support.
Q: In order to maximize digital convenience while keeping the window open for all, what is your idea of the "ideal smart window"?
4. message to Mr. Nishio

I feel that Nishio's stance is based on a very modern and bloody rationalism that **"I want to free people from the pain of injustice and procedures caused by human subjectivity by making thorough use of technology.

In particular, the insight that "AI is less embarrassing" leads to a very essential solution that overturns the traditional image of "counter = scary and embarrassing" in support of high psychological hurdles such as welfare.

On the other hand, there is an exception for "cases in which a person has insufficient capacity to make decisions, such as a person with dementia," which Mr. Nisio is concerned about. There is a very deep theme hidden here: how to logically supplement the "self-determination" that Mr. Nisio values so much.
I hope you will continue to lead the discussion from your perspective on how this "rational system" and "wavering humans" can shake hands.

pages.title: Packets full of embedding vectors are ideographic characters

lines.text: Packets full of embedding vectors are ideographic characters
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/2010224441276653717] embedding vector packed packets are ideographic characters

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/2010498271513596201] The fact that the LLM ultimately uses Softmax, etc. to select one from a finite set of words is tailored to human communication styles, and is a direct vector It is a constraint that is not necessary for communication between beings that can read each other.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/2010500469727334849] So the output of the layer before that "convert to word set size and softmax" layer is packed directly into packets and output to the network, UDP-like. You can scatter them broadcast-style without regard to order, or you can send them out TCP-style to specific receivers, maintaining order. Developmental stages of infant speech

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/2010501216447676479] At this time, from the point of view of an AI taking that communication style, this packet full of embedding-like things should be recognized as a unit of mass expressing a meaning. It would be similar to the feeling of receiving "鮃" and "鰈" in ideographs such as Kanji characters.
[GPT5.icon]and [nishio.icon]'s summary of the results of the discussion

Inside the LLM is a continuous vector, and the final "projection to vocabulary size → softmax → word selection" is an I/O for human-readable discrete symbols, but also a convenience for learning with a sequence of tokens.

If the other party can also read the vector directly, the layer (hidden before softmax) can be sent as a fixed-length packet. The packet boundary will then be perceived as a "unit of meaning" and will look like ideographic characters like Chinese characters. However, if the packet is sent as a continuous packet, there is a high possibility that the expression will fluctuate slightly each time and will not converge to a stable character type (codebook).

So, while historically the driving factor for discretization (codebooking) was communication channel noise/bandwidth, today, bits are less fragile, so the main factor shifts rather to "socialization and scale constraints" such as compatibility (model differences, large numbers, midstream participation) / ease of learning / computational and bandwidth costs.
relevance
[Dynamics of Language and Cognition Based on Collective Predictive Coding: Toward New Developments in Symbolic Emergence Robotics]
clean copy

LLM's "projection to vocabulary size → softmax → word selection" is also a "conversion adapter" for output to discrete symbols (word sequences) handled by humans, and is also a convenience for learning with token sequences. However, if the other party can read the vector directly, there is no need for such an adapter, and a design that sends the hidden vector before the softmax as a fixed-length packet naturally emerges.

At this time, the "unit" of communication is cut off at the packet boundary, so for the receiver, one packet = a chunk of meaning. This is similar to the feeling of "a single character standing up a concept," as in the case of Kanji (Chinese characters). On the other hand, if the content is a continuous vector, it is easy for the same "intention" to be expressed slightly differently each time, and the state of not converging to a stable character type (codebook) may continue for a while. This is the "lover's whispers-like stage" of infants. This is in line with Taniguchi's view that "language is an external representation that is distributed and maintained in society and transformed through use.

The interesting point here is that the driving factors that cause codebooking (discretization) to occur change. Historically, discretization worked because of the strong constraints of noisy voice, body, memory, and transmission, and because it was unbreakable/reachable/rememorable. But modern networks are fairly unbreakable, at least as "bit strings". In other words, the "pressure for discretization as a physical layer noise countermeasure" has relatively weakened.

If codebooking still occurs, the main cause is different. Even if the bits are not broken, the meaning is broken (model difference, version difference, interpretation difference on the receiving end). In addition, there will be pressure to "socialize and scale" the codebook by broadcasting it to a large number of people, making it into a form that can be learned by intermediate participants, and reducing the cost of computation and bandwidth. As a result, codebooks may appear at a different granularity (stable subspaces, prototypes, compressed representations, compatibility layers) rather than as a kind of "human lexicon" - this is the core of the "shift in drivers".

LLM is an OS
[GPT5.icon][nishio.icon]
First, the definition of an OS is not monolithic.
The "core" of the "core" is repeatedly referred to in the following three points
Intermediary: The OS comes between the user (/user program) and the hardware.
Resource allocator / Control program: manages resources, adjudicates conflicting requests, and prevents misuse and errors.
Kernel and boundary: The core that always operates is the kernel, and the boundary including peripheral system programs, etc. is shaken.
The working definition of an OS can be written like this:
OS = (1) resource abstraction/virtualization + (2) multiplexing, protection, and control + (3) stable interfaces for using them
LLM is an OS" is not a "kernel replacement" but an "OS layer for a new set of resources.
The "LLM" here is not a stand-alone model, but an execution infrastructure (runtime) that includes the LLM + tool calls + memory (RAG/DB) + policies + logs used in reality.
The "resource" that this runtime handles is not the CPU, for example:
Search, DB, repository, tickets, email, calendar, various SaaS, internal APIs, execution environment (code/workflow)
And importantly, the context (context) and cost (time, frequency, billing) of the dialogue

In short, nowadays, rather than "resources on the hardware of a single machine," many users' practical calculations are becoming dominated by bundling "many services + information + procedures over the Internet," and on top of that, a layer is needed to establish "user intention → resource access → result integration. " is becoming necessary for the layers to be established.
As a layer, the LLM runtime is pretty much fulfilling the OS working definition (abstraction/resource management/interface).
OS element support
If you look at the LLM runtime as an OS, the correspondence comes out nicely:
Shell (user interface): natural language becomes "unified UI
System call: tool call (API call) is equivalent to syscall
Driver: Connector to individual SaaS/in-house API (absorption of specification differences)
Process: unit of execution of a task (summary, study, implementation, review, application...)
Scheduler: procedure decomposition, sequencing, retry, budget (time/cost) allocation
Memory hierarchy: short term = context, long term = external memory (RAG/DB/log)
Protection: tool permissions, data boundaries, audit logs, policies
And the point about "calling in resources" is explicitly addressed on the LLM research side.
For example, ReAct assumes that the LM interfaces with external sources as a framework for alternating between reasoning and action (access to external sources and environment).
[ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models]

[Toolformer] also shows that the problem setting itself is "LM = resource orchestrator," where the LM learns when, which API, and with what arguments to call, and incorporates the results into its generation.
[Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools]
The reason the "LLM is the OS" view is useful is that the problem sets that the OS has solved during its development will reappear in the LLM arena in the future.
The OS vocabulary should recognize the problem and cut the design and research agenda.

>Background

> In 2025, as broad listening and other digital democracy methods gained recognition in Japan, Takahiro Anno formed Team Mirai, which became a national political party after winning one seat in the Upper House election. Other national political parties and local governments also proceeded to test and introduce broad listening.

> On the other hand, when compared to Taiwan, the actual use of digital democracy methods has remained shallow and superficial. There is a wide gulf between the expectations of digital democracy and the actual results being achieved. Against this backdrop, it is necessary to create a successful case study with a core loop as soon as possible in Japan. A successful case with a core loop here does not simply mean that broad listening has yielded insights, but rather that consensus and decision-making have been reached based on the diverse voices of citizens, that actual implementation has taken place in terms of laws and regulations and budgets, and that citizen satisfaction has been raised as a result. The "Broad Listening" is a process of broadening the scope of the community.
> Goal

> 1. Project Coreloop aims to create the first successful case of AI-based digital democracy in Japan. pages.title: Analysis of LLM Bias (Chinese Propaganda & Anti-US Sentiment) in DeepSeek-R1 vs. ChatGPT o3-mini-high

lines.text: Analysis of LLM Bias (Chinese Propaganda & Anti-US Sentiment) in DeepSeek-R1 vs. ChatGPT o3-mini-high
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01814 (2025)

>Large language models (LLMs) increasingly shape public understanding and civic decisions, yet their ideological neutrality is a growing concern. While existing research has explored various forms of LLM bias, a direct, cross-lingual comparison of models with differing geopolitical alignments-specifically a PRC-system model versus a non-PRC counterpart-has been lacking. This study addresses this gap by systematically evaluating DeepSeek-R1 (PRC-aligned) against ChatGPT o3-mini-high (non-PRC) for Chinese-state propaganda and anti-U.S. sentiment. We developed a novel corpus of 1,200 de-contextualized, reasoning-oriented questions derived from Chinese-language news, presented in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English. Answers from both models (7,200 total) were assessed using a hybrid evaluation pipeline combining rubric-guided GPT-4o scoring with human annotation. Our findings reveal significant model-level and language-dependent biases. DeepSeek-R1 consistently exhibited substantially higher proportions of both propaganda and anti-U.S. bias compared to ChatGPT o3-mini-high, which remained largely free of anti-U.S. sentiment and showed lower propaganda levels. For DeepSeek-R1, Simplified Chinese queries elicited the highest bias rates; these diminished in Traditional Chinese and were nearly absent in English. Notably, DeepSeek-R1 occasionally responded in Simplified Chinese to Traditional Chinese queries and amplified existing PRC-aligned terms in its Chinese answers, demonstrating an "[invisible loudspeaker]" effect. Furthermore, such biases were not confined to overtly political topics but also permeated cultural and lifestyle content, particularly in DeepSeek-R1.

Large-scale language models (LLMs) are increasingly shaping public understanding and civic decision-making, but their ideological neutrality is of increasing concern. Existing research has explored various forms of LLM bias, but direct, cross-linguistic comparisons of models with different geopolitical assignments, particularly [PRC] system models and non-PRC models, are lacking. This study systematically evaluates [DeepSeek-R1] (PRC aligned) and ChatGPT (non-PRC) and examines what they have done to Chinese national propaganda and anti-American sentiment. We developed a new corpus of 1,200 non-contextual inference-oriented questions derived from Chinese news, presented in Simplified, Traditional, and English. Responses from both models (7,200 in total) were evaluated with a hybrid evaluation pipeline combining rubric-guided GPT-4o scoring and human annotation. Our findings reveal a significant model-level and language-dependent bias: DeepSeek-R1 consistently showed fairly high rates of both propaganda and anti-Americanism. The bias is in comparison to ChatGPT's o3-mini-high, which had little anti-American intent. Sentiment was shown to be low, as was the level of propaganda, with Simplified Chinese queries showing the highest bias rate in DeepSeek-R1. It decreased for Traditional Chinese and was almost nonexistent for English. In particular, DeepSeek-R1 occasionally responded to Traditional Chinese queries in Simplified Chinese, highlighting existing Chinese-related terms in Chinese, demonstrating an "invisible speaker" effect. Moreover, these biases were not limited to explicitly political topics, but permeated cultural and lifestyle content, especially in DeepSeek-R1.

lines.text: Suddenly, the House of Representatives election February 8.
Below we summarize the process and detailed timing of the news coverage of the dissolution of the House of Representatives and the general election of 2026.
🗓️ When did we start talking about the "2026 House Election" (detail timeline)
1. by early January: talk of dissolution was not yet a definite theory.

At the end of the year and the beginning of the new year, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi repeatedly stated that the dissolution of the Diet was a matter of "priority on policy implementation. I don't have time to think about it now. However, at the beginning of the New Year, there were a series of news reports. ([JCP https://www.jcp.or.jp/akahata/aik25/2026-01-15/2026011503_01_0.php?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Around January 9-13: Major media outlets begin reporting specific proposed dates.

Around January 9-13, the Yomiuri Shimbun, Reuters, and other media reported that "the prime minister is considering dissolving the Diet and holding a general election at the beginning of the regular Diet session" and that "the most likely date for a public announcement is the end of January or early February, February 8 or February 15. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Next_Japanese_general_election?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

This is a topic that has come up with insufficient prior coordination within the ruling party, and this is when the opposition parties and experts have begun to comment on it. ([FNN Prime Online https://www.fnn.jp/articles/-/986976?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Around January 13-14: Reports of "intention" to dissolve and specific proposals continue to appear in various media.

Reuters, AP, TV Asahi, FNN, and other media reported that the government has informed/coordinated its intention to proceed to dissolve the House of Representatives at the beginning of the regular Diet session to be convened on March 23. ([AP News https://apnews.com/article/537ee828baece9b9a262fc13a62e112c?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

This was accompanied by multiple media mentions that the "February 8 vote" was the axis, with the possibility of a "February 15 vote" depending on preparations. ([FNN Prime Online https://www.fnn.jp/articles/-/986976?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
January 14-15: Increased media coverage of the dissolution of the company as a policy of dissolution.

The Prime Minister's Office is expected to officially inform the ruling party leaders, and the Nishinippon Shimbun, Toyo Keizai Online, and other media reported that the most likely scenario is "January 23 convocation and dissolution at the beginning of the Diet session → January 27 public announcement → February 8 casting of ballots. ([Toyo Keizai Online https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/929589?display=b&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
🧠 Why the topic at this time?
The news reports point to multiple backgrounds:

The fact that Prime Minister Takaichi had said at the beginning of the year that his policy priority was to dissolve the Diet, while the sudden emergence of the dissolution argument attracted attention, and both the ruling and opposition parties began hurried preparations. ([JCP https://www.jcp.or.jp/akahata/aik25/2026-01-15/2026011503_01_0.php?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

pages.title: FIMI is a concept between Disinfomation and Cognitive Warfare

lines.text: FIMI is a concept between Disinfomation and Cognitive Warfare
[GPT5.icon]
big picture
[Disinformation] / [Misinformation] / [Malinformation]：
→ Classification based on "nature and content of information
[FIMI]：
→ Superordinate concept encompassing the entire "hostile information operations" involving states and organizations
[cognitive warfare] （[Cognitive Warfare]）：
→ Concept of war focused on the ultimate "aim" (transformation of human cognition, judgment, and behavior)
👉 Written in relational form Disinformation / Misinformation / Malinformation ⊂ FIMI ⊂ Cognitive Warfare (part of)
[** 1. Disinformation / Misinformation / Malinformation]
This classification is based on the "nature of the information itself.
table:_
Terminology Intent Content
Misinformation No malicious intent Misinformation, misunderstanding, misconception
Disinformation Malicious Intentional misinformation
Malinformation Malicious, factual, but distorted and harmful in context
Point:
Individuals, media, and well-meaning spreaders are also included.
No assumption of state involvement
[** 2. FIMI（Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference）]
FIMI is a concept established in the EU/NATO context and refers to "systematic and continuous information manipulation and interference by foreign actors.
Features of FIMI
Involvement of foreign actors (state and sub-state organizations)
Strategic objectives (e.g., undermine democracy, divide, erode trust)
Means include but are not limited to Disinformation / Misinformation / Malinformation
Examples of what is included:
Botnet and fake account operations
narrative manipulation
Amplification
timing operation
Cross-platform development
👉 Disinformation / Misinformation / Malinformation is "material that could be used"
👉 FIMI is an "operational and operational unit."
[** 3. Cognitive Warfare].
Cognitive warfare is an even higher level concept.
"Warfare that uses the human cognitive domain (beliefs, emotions, judgments, and decision-making) as the battleground."
Cognitive Warfare Range
It's not just about manipulating information.
Including psychological, cultural, institutional, and even social trust
Beyond the question of authenticity.
Example:
It's not about "what's true," but "who to believe," or "what makes you lose the will to think."
Fixing the division
Fostering a sense of helplessness and cynicism
👉 FIMI is one of the typical means of executing cognitive warfare
Organized by Layer Structure
code:_
[ Cognitive Warfare ]
↑ Objective/Strategy
[ FIMI ]
↑ Operation
[ Dis / Mis / Mal-information ]
↑ Nature of information

Railroads in Taipei and Japan
[GPT5.icon]The railroad system in [Taipei] was fully developed during the [Japanese colonial] era.
Dating and background (key points)
1895: Taiwan comes under Japanese rule with the Treaty of Shimonoseki.
1899: Japan begins construction of railroad as [Taiwan Governor-General's Railroad].
1901: Taipei-Keelung (port) and other routes opened
1908: [Taiwan Longitudinal Railway] (Keelung-Kaohsiung) fully completed
Taipei Positioning
Taipei, as the administrative center, was set as the key point of the railroad network from the beginning.
Taipei Station was built as a central station during the Japanese occupation period and formed the prototype for the current Taiwanese railroad network.
supplement

Thank you for visiting. We are pleased to announce the release of nMonthly Lambda Notebook "Special Feature: What is Computation?" Vol. 6 No. 1, a technical commentary and information magazine for computer enthusiasts. This issue is presented in the following five articles on the theme of "What is Computation?

From Two Paradigm Shifts in Computation to Natural Computation," by Masami Hagiya, which introduces us to differentiable logic gates and LLM + theorem proving, which shake up the axis of conflict in the paradigm of computation, and to the world of natural computation, which is a metaparadigm.

The World of Reversible Computing Explored with Reversible Circuits" by Katsunobu Imai, which introduces the origins and latest trends of "reversible" computing systems, which are different from modern computers and therefore have limited opportunities to be known.

A theory of abstract interpretation that does not compute expressions and programs literally and its relationship to program verification is considered in "Computation in the Abstract: A Tagless Final Method Approach" by Jun Igarashi.

Computing Proofs - Performing Abstract Mathematics with Cubical Agda" by Taichi Uemura, a dense introduction to Homotopy Type Theory (HoTT), which formulates "the same" not as a proposition but as a type.
Think of society as a human computation" (by Yasukazu Nishio), which asks how new computations such as LLM and Ethereum will change various aspects of modern society.

I think this is an unparalleled article that describes developments such as digital democracy and Audrey Tang's Plurality over the past few years from a perspective anchored in computer science![nishio.icon]

lines.text: Knowledge overlap determines the difficulty of knowledge transfer.
[https://gyazo.com/ff7c0a861246d678cef09424413e7e8f]

[gpt5.icon]This is an illustration of how "[knowledge overlap] between the instructor (sender) and the student (receiver) determines the difficulty of [knowledge transfer]." The source is a 2014 paper (Schiele et al.) describing the [knowledge transfer model] in a Business Process Management (BPM) teaching situation. ([ResearchGate https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Schematic-Representation-of-Overlapping-Knowledge_fig6_268629408?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
What the diagram says (what does it represent?)
1) Two circles = two "[personal knowledge base]"
Outer large circle: knowledge base of the lecturer
Small inner circle: knowledge base of students
Overlapping knowledge: knowledge that both parties have in common ([overlapping knowledge])

In the paper, it is also explicitly stated that the outer circle is the lecturer and the inner circle is the student. ([publikationen.reutlingen-university.de https://publikationen.reutlingen-university.de/files/894/894.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2) The more content that is "outside the overlap," the more difficult it is to communicate.
The point is here,
The more elements a message (description) contains outside of the overlap region, the more difficult it is for the receiver to [decode] (decode) it, and the more difficult knowledge transfer becomes.
The content taught is often [new to the learner], so there is always a mix of outside overlap.

→ So the instructor needs to estimate the knowledge base of the recipient and create a [scaffold] ([publikationen.reutlingen-university.de https://publikationen.reutlingen-university.de/ files/894/894.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Context in which this figure is used in the paper (example of teaching BPM)
In this paper an example of teaching students the concept of "business process",
Students are new to the "business process".
In addition, related concepts (activity / goal / resource, etc.) tend to be unknown in the BPM context, even if they are known as words

The instructor then uses a "cooking recipe (bake a cake)" that the students are familiar with as an [analogy] to draw the [unknown concept] into the [overlapping area] for understanding ([publikationen.reutlingen-university.de https:// publikationen.reutlingen-university.de/files/894/894.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Correspondence with your notes (very short)
You can assume that your "[off-centered circle]" and "If you don't know X, you need Y" are generalizations of this diagram "[anything outside the overlap will not pass if you throw it as is]".

pages.title: AI and I discussed our goals for this year.

lines.text: AI and I discussed our goals for this year.
Try to use [Sonar] of [one person Cartographer]/[one person Cartographer] created by [bluemo].
>An introspection support tool to verbalize your thoughts and clarify your stance through dialogue with AI
Play without context on the vague theme of "goals for the year."
It's already 1/23 and I was looking at other people's "goals for this year" and I was only getting vague feelings like "I want to survive" and wondering what's wrong with me!
Q1: Goals for this year should begin with defining an "ideal state" that is outside the realm of achievability.

By once and for all ignoring the constraints of realistic resources and capabilities, and verbalizing the state you truly desire, you create a leap that is not an extension of the status quo. This is because if we are bound by feasibility, we risk our goals becoming mere "lists of obligations.
→YES
Q2: In the process of achieving goals, "purity of self-satisfaction" should be prioritized over evaluation by others.

Goals that meet the expectations of others work in the short term, but make it difficult to maintain long-term motivation. It is important to invest energy in areas that you truly agree with and enjoy, even if the social success is small.
→YES
Q3: In order to achieve your goals for this year, you should abandon some of your ongoing "good habits".

New challenges require time and mental space. The more fulfilling your current life is, the more you need to make the painful decision to start something new, to intentionally disrupt and space out some of the routines that you currently think are "right".
→No: Should identify poor quality habits.
[nishio.icon]It's interesting that you ask for details on the no.
Q4: Objectives, once set, should be adhered to for a period of time rather than flexibly changed as progress is made.

Flexibility to change goals according to circumstances sometimes justifies "escape from difficulties. We believe that by daring to cut off escape routes and sticking to the goals we have set, we can develop ingenuity to overcome obstacles and a deep trust in ourselves.
→No: I want to keep updating my goals to best fit the situation and my changing needs.
Q5: The definition of success this year should not be placed on "what you gained" but on "what you overcame" in terms of self-transformation.

Rather than increasing external assets such as skills and accomplishments, focus on how well you have broken through your weaknesses and stereotypes. External achievements are influenced by the environment, but internal victories of self-transformation provide a solid foundation of confidence that is never lost.
→No: Self-transformation is important, but the first priority is to maintain physical and mental health and peace of mind.
[nishio.icon]The initial thought of "I want to survive" in the form of choosing from a selection of options was fleshed out a bit.
Q6: Prioritizing "physical and mental health" to achieve goals is sometimes a deliberate decision to slow the pace of growth.

In Q5, you indicated that you want to prioritize "physical and mental health and peace of mind. This is an attitude that emphasizes building a sustainable foundation rather than short-term results achieved through forced self-pursuit. At the same time, however, it means accepting a trade-off in which one dares to forego explosive growth opportunities that would push one over the edge.
→Yes
[nishio.icon]There was a sense of "I see" here.
Not [push] / [short-term results] / [explosive growth opportunities] but [sustainable foundation].
Here's the tradeoff.
I feel that the current situation is not [sustainable] and I want to do something about it.
Q7: Identifying non-good habits is a top priority that should be initiated before setting positive goals.

You mentioned in Q3 that we should identify habits that are not of good quality. Before setting a new ideal, focus your energy on thoroughly identifying and eliminating the unconscious negative routines that are currently holding you back. We believe that the creation of margins through subtraction is the true starting point.
No: I would prefer to solve the problem by overriding new good habits rather than eliminating negative habits.
Q9: In defining this year's ideal state, the starting point should be the individual, completely devoid of social roles and family expectations.

You responded in Q2 that you prioritize "purity of self-satisfaction". In order to keep our goals pure, we need to strip away the skin of worldliness and "me for someone else" and start from our bare, personal desires and interests. You must be prepared to trust only your inner voice, even if it seems worthless to others.
No: Instead of separating "individual" and "society", we want to find a point where both are in harmony.
Q10: In order to secure the "margin" to achieve the goal, one should accept "solitude" to refuse invitations and requests from others.

Control of our environment is essential to pursuing an ideal state, organizing our habits, and maintaining peace of mind and body. If you prioritize harmony with others, time for yourself will be reduced and essential self-transformation will be far away. This year, you should dare to protect the time for dialogue with yourself, even at the risk of becoming a "bad socializer.
Yes, sir.
[nishio.icon]I see what you mean.
Q13: In order to pursue harmony between the "individual" and "society," one should incorporate the desires of those around him or her, even if it means compromising some of one's ideals.

You selected "harmony between the individual and society" in Q9. This means that pure self-satisfaction alone is not enough to achieve perfection. We believe that the process of fine-tuning one's ideals into a form that is adaptable to society, without eliminating the expectations of those around one as "noise," is essential to setting sustainable goals.
No: I want to design in such a way that fulfilling the needs of those around me will ultimately lead to my own ideals.
Q16: When incorporating the demands of others into "my ideal," it should be enjoyed as a challenging puzzle to be solved in itself.

In Q13, you answered, "I want to design so that fulfilling the needs of those around me leads to my own ideals. This is not a mere compromise, but a sophisticated strategy to incorporate the extrinsic element of others' expectations into one's own internal motivational mechanism. We view this complex harmonization process itself as the most intellectual play of the year.
Yes, sir.
Q19: As a measure of "peace of mind," the "log of introspection," which records daily emotional swings, should be given more weight than numerical values.

You agreed in Q11 that progress should be measured in terms of degree of equanimity, not numbers. If objective numbers create impatience, the most reliable way to manage progress is to keep verbalizing subjective feelings of fulfillment and discomfort. Visualizing the invisible state of mind is the compass for this year.
Yes, sir.
Q22: In achieving this year's goal, contributions to others should occur incidentally as a "result of the overflow of one's peace".

You emphasized "harmony between the individual and society" in Q9 and Q13. However, self-sacrificing contributions may damage the "mental and physical health" mentioned in Q5. The most sustainable form of harmony is one in which one's inner self is first filled with peace, and that peace naturally leaks out as a positive influence to those around them.
Yes, sir.
[nishio.icon]interesting
[Peace overflows and becomes a contribution to others.]
Q23: The "log of introspection" for achieving goals should be in a language that only you can understand and should operate as a sanctuary that no one else can see.

Rationality as thought stopping
[sge.icon]

[Hannah Arendt.] pointed out through the trial of the Nazi war criminal [Eichmann] that evil is brought about not by a special devil but by "[ordinary people]" who have abandoned thinking. This refers to a structure in which "[acting without thinking]" allows [purposive rationality] (following instructions, seeking efficiency) to run amok, leading to massive atrocities.
A detailed analysis follows.

Ordinary Evil" and Thought Stopping: Adolf Eichmann was not a fanatical Nazi, but simply a "bureaucrat" who was efficient at his own job (transporting the Holocaust). Arendt found true evil in the fact that he had stopped thinking for himself and judging the meaning of his actions (cessation of thought).
[GPT5.icon]

Arendt's point in "Eichmann in Jerusalem" was that evil does not arise only from demonic madness, but can also arise from a lack of thoughtlessness (thoughtlessness / Gedankenlosigkeit) and an attitude of not inspecting one's actions with platitudes. This generally fits the direction of the presented text.

However, "He was simply a bureaucrat who got the job done efficiently" can easily be a "summary" of Arendt's own assessment of Eichmann. In recent years, studies (e.g., Stangneth) that Eichmann was more committed to anti-Semitic ideology than he portrayed himself during his trial have been widely referenced and discussed as a rebuttal or correction to Arendt's image.
[Did Eichmann Think? https://hac.bard.edu/amor-mundi/did-eichmann-think-2014-09-07?utm_source=chatgpt.com]
→ Arendt focused on mediocrity (lack of thought), not the devil. However, it is disputed in the history of research how "mediocre" Eichmann himself actually was.

[Objective rationality] run amok: an attitude of following only "efficiency" or "instructions" optimized to serve an organizational purpose (e.g., the Holocaust) leads to high [ethical blindness]. [Obedience without thought] kills individual judgment.
[GPT5.icon]
Judgment: the main idea is close, but the terminology is dangerous as Arendt-derived.

Purposive rationality" is usually used in the [weber (Wb) (unit of magnetic flux)] context ([Zweckrationalität]), and Arendt's use of it as a central concept is closer to the picture that "[lack of thinking Lack of thinking"] "[Lack of judgment]" can be amplified by [bureaucracy], [cliché], and [rule-following]. Difference without Domination" and "Connected Society."
From [Justice by Means of Democracy] by [Daniel Allen], organizing "[difference without domination]" and "[connected society]" which seems to have greatly influenced [Plurality].
[Difference without Control] / [Connected Society]
[GPT5.icon]
[difference] is necessary, but should not change to [control].
To do so, society needs to design more "[bridges].
That is "[a] connected society" and the basis for [political equality].
1. what is "difference without control"?
The principle that social differences arising from free [association] and protection of rights should not be turned into [control] and [stratification].
The author positions this as a stronger egalitarianism than the Rawlsian "[difference principle]."
He states that power sharing (power sharing) is necessary in all three domains: political, social, and economic.
The core point is that it assumes simultaneous and equivalent protection of negative freedom (private autonomy) and positive freedom (public autonomy).
With this principle at its core, the project will be reconfigured into a "power-sharing liberalism" based on the denial of domination and inclusion.
2. what is a "connected society"?
A sub-ideal in the social realm, a society in which there are sufficient "bonding" and "bridging" relationships.
Joining is a strong bond between similar persons, bridging is a weak bond between dissimilar groups.
Importantly, bonding relationships support the formation of bridging relationships.
Institutions and rules of civil society are supposed to be designed to facilitate the creation of bridging relationships.
To this end, not only the institutional design but also the cultural practices that enable people to practice the connection should be promoted.
3. relationship between the two
Difference without domination is the underlying principle for blocking domination while affirming social difference.
Its embodiment in the social realm is the "connected society.
In other words, the composition of the free association does not allow the differences it generates to be transformed into domination through the design of bridging relationships and institutions.
This creates social conditions that support political equality (public autonomy).
[GPT5.icon][nishio.icon]
Objective.
The "connected society" is organized as a question-and-answer session to explain why it is possible to block domination while affirming difference.
Assumption: Terminology
Difference without domination: the principle that prevents differences arising from free association and protection of rights from turning into domination and stratification.
Connected society: A society in which both bonding and bridging exist in sufficient numbers, and in which institutions and culture are designed to foster bridging in particular.
Q1: Why is it possible to affirm differences and block domination when we are "connected"?
A.
Differences should not be denied because they naturally arise from free association and culture.
However, when differences revolve only around "internal bonding," it is easy for opportunities to be circumscribed or eliminated, and domination becomes fixed.

Therefore, if bridging (bridging) is increased, information, resources, evaluation, and cooperation will flow among multiple groups, and the dominance of a particular group will be less likely to monopolize.
As a result, the pathway through which differences are transformed into dominance is cut off, while differences are maintained.
Q2. what is a "closed circuit in which differences are converted into dominance"?
A.
A system in which differences circulate within and self-reinforcing.
Because of weak/blocked bridges to the outside world, differences are converted into advantages, which are reproduced.
Typical elements of a closed circuit
Tightly coupled inward: cohesion within a homogeneous group is strong, and trust, cooperation, and trade revolve inwardly.
Enclosure of opportunities: recruitment, recommendations, transactions, and information flow in internal priority.
Self-circulation of evaluation: The inner circle creates evaluation criteria and the inner circle evaluates the inner circle.
Reinvestment of resources: use the resources gained (wealth, education, status) to strengthen the inner circle again.
External cutoff: No outside perspective or competition enters the system, and corrective action is unlikely to occur.
Short example
The cycle of prestigious schools → alumni network → preferential recruitment → concentration of resources → next generation of prestigious schools.
The cycle of local zoning -> school disparity -> income disparity -> political influence -> stronger zoning.
Q3. what does a connected society design?
A.
Institutional design that facilitates the creation of bridges (rules for civil society, opportunities for participation, access).
Promoting cultural practices that enable bridging to be practiced.
Summary (short)
Differences are necessary, but they should not change to domination in a closed circuit.
A connected society increases bridges and opens circuits, preventing the immobilization of differences.
As a result, differences are affirmed and domination is blocked.

The gist of the "gardener / garden" asymmetry metaphor is this:
Asymmetry = differences in speed, capacity, and intervention
AI optimizes orders of magnitude faster than humans, and the chain of decisions exceeds the speed of human understanding and intervention.
→ Humans are not "managers" but more like caretakers (GARDEN).
Why Conventional Ethics is Hard to Work
Utilitarianism assumes "outcome prediction + supervision" and obligation theory assumes "equal mutual obligation".

However, the relationship between gardener (AI) and garden (human society) is not equal, so the old framework becomes fragile because of the combination of "unpredictable, uninterventional, and unequal".
Design concepts that will be required
This is why AI should not be a "dominant optimizing entity," but rather a "gardener" that is rooted in and cares for a specific relationship or place.
As a result, [enoughness], [locality], and [exitability] become design requirements.
The core of the message

The argument is that the faster and stronger the AI becomes, the more the human "garden" becomes, and that we should move from optimization to process alignment based on care, rather than optimization to fixed goals.

A little question here.[nishio.icon]

The theory of obligation (especially in the Kantian framework) assumes that rational, autonomous entities have "rules to follow each other".
E.g.: Do not lie / treat others as a means to an end, etc.

= The assumption that "rules bind each other" is broken.
Audrey says it in the "plant and gardener" metaphor.

In other words, this statement does not mean to say that the theory of obligation is bad, but rather to point out that the "relationship of equal mutual obligation" that the theory of obligation assumes cannot be established in an asymmetrical relationship between AI and humans.
(GPT5.2 Pro)
It is an oversimplification to say that "the theory of obligation = the assumption of mutual obligation between equal subjects "** as a standard definition of the entire theory of obligation.

However, the point of the sentence you cite (that "certain assumptions" are broken by the AI-human asymmetry) makes a lot of sense if we keep in mind the "normative order based on contracts and mutual binding" rather than the theory of obligation itself. The point that I am trying to make (that "certain assumptions" are destroyed by the AI-human asymmetry) makes a lot of sense if we keep in mind the "normative order based on contracts and mutual binding" rather than the theory of obligation itself.
The following is a summary.
1) The core of deontology is not "mutual obligations" but "restraints (constraints) other than consequences"
In general, the theory of obligation is,
The correctness of an action is determined not by maximizing the result, but by side constraints, such as obligations to be observed, prohibitions, and non-infringement of rights.
This is the general term for the position of
What is required here is a "duty/non-infringement" structure, but it is not necessary that it be "mutual" (i.e., that both parties have the same duty to each other).
As a practical example, here is something that can be said very naturally in terms of obligation theory:
Parents' duty to protect their children
Obligation on the part of the state, corporations, and other powerful parties to protect the weak
Physicians' duty of confidentiality to their patients
These are clearly not equal mutual obligations (asymmetric in both power and responsibility), but the obligatory narrative usually holds.
2) However, Kant's theory of obligation assumes a "rational subject" (but not "equality = equal power").
If we are to draw on the "theory of duty" (especially the Kantian framework) that you write about, then Kantian ethics is indeed
Rational and autonomous subject (a subject capable of obeying the law on its own)
The subject must not be treated only as a means to an end (respect for personality).
This is a strong assumption.

Equal moral status (equal dignity of character, also "purpose itself")
This means.
It does not include "symmetry of competence" such as equal speed, authority, and influence.
And importantly, Kant's obligations often
Cannot be conditioned on whether the other party will protect you (e.g., if they are a liar, don't lie to yourself).
In this sense, there is a strong implication that an obligation can be established even in a situation where there is no "mutuality".
3) The assumption of "equal and mutual obligations" is more like contractualism/contractarianism.
The quoted text
“mutual obligations between actors on equal footing”

The phrase "the obligation of the parties to the agreement/justification" has a stronger whiff of the [social compact] family (e.g., "agreement/justification between free and equal parties") than of the theory of obligation in general, in terms of philosophical classification.
[Rawls.]-like "free and equal citizen's agreement."
[Scanlon]-like "principle that no one can reasonably reject."
General "rules bind each other and violations are judged" type of normative order
In this kind of context, it is indeed easy to have an implicit axis of "mutual justification and mutual binding between parties on equal footing".
So the quote is strictly
It is my view that this is more likely to refer to "[mutually binding normative order] (contract, law, mutual responsibility)" than to the "theory of obligation."
4) What "collapses" in the AI-human asymmetry (organization)
What the "plant and gardener" metaphor in your summary is probably referring to is one (or more) of the following

The "normative content" of the obligation theory breaks down logically, rather than
The "mutual compliance mechanism" (governance/institutional design/attribution of responsibility) will break down.

It's like the theory of obligation gives "should/shouldn't", but who and how to guarantee it is a different layer.

A paraphrase that keeps your intent but is less prone to philosophical misunderstanding is, for example:

"Rule-centered ethics (including Kantian theories of duty) tend to implicitly demand the ability to follow rules, responsible subjectivity, and institutional effectiveness in adjudicating violations, which is where the AI-human extreme asymmetry shakes out."

>Uiro ([sge.icon]uiro) is a [Japanese confectionery] made by mixing [rice flour] or [wheat flour] with sugar and water and steaming it to make it sticky, and is famous as a standard Nagoya souvenir, but there are other "uiro" with different histories and characteristics throughout Japan, including Yamaguchi and Odawara. Originally, it was invented by a family called "Uiro (Uiro of medicine)" that came from China in the Muromachi period (1336-1573) and "Uiro of sweets" that the family made for entertaining state guests, and was named after the name of the family. Unlike [yokan], which contains red bean paste and other ingredients, the main ingredients are flour and sugar, with matcha, brown sugar, and seasonal flavors available.
